still_open.note: Still open. git ls-files NaruServe-servlet is empty; the directory exists only because of NaruServe-servlet/build. A fresh clone hits the Gradle 'project without an existing directory' deprecation, which becomes an error in Gradle 9. The fix is a tracked placeholder source, outside this lane's write set.

findings.title: TestKit now runs in the developer's real Gradle user home, so nested builds lose hermeticity
findings.description: withTestKitDir(gradle.gradleUserHomeDir) makes the outer ~/.gradle the Gradle user home of every nested build. That fixes the cache and offline problem (FND-004). But the nested builds now also pick up ~/.gradle/gradle.properties (for example org.gradle.configuration-cache, org.gradle.parallel, org.gradle.jvmargs, org.gradle.warning.mode) and ~/.gradle/init.d scripts. Several negative cases assert exact output: sdsAc4 asserts that no '> Task' line appears, others assert that specific messages are present. A user-level init script or property can change that output and break or mask those cases on one machine but not another. The fixer names this trade-off in fix_iter1.json, but nothing in the code guards against it, and no comment records it beyond the cache rationale.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a dedicated TestKit dir (a build-dir path) and share only the dependency cache, read-only: pass GRADLE_RO_DEP_CACHE=<outer user home>/caches through GradleRunner.withEnvironment. Or keep the shared home and add a 'shortcut:' comment naming the init.d and gradle.properties exposure.

findings.title: The new nested-dir test passes trivially unless the outer build overrides tinyHttpdDir
findings.description: With the default path, the outer and nested builds resolve the same directory whether or not -PtinyHttpdDir is forwarded. The test then shows nothing about FND-001 in the default ./gradlew build. It catches a regression only when the run is invoked with a non-default override, and no CI or documented command does that.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the test independent of the outer invocation: give the temp copy a settings default that points to a non-existent path, or assert that runner()'s argument list contains -PtinyHttpdDir=<property>. Or document a CI step that runs with a relative override.

findings.title: The override check recognizes only the '-PtinyHttpdDir=' spelling
findings.description: A caller that writes '-P', 'tinyHttpdDir=...' as separate arguments, or '--project-prop', gets a second -PtinyHttpdDir appended. Which value wins then depends on argument order. Today every caller uses the '-P...=' form, so nothing breaks yet.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave as is, or add a one-line comment saying callers must use the '-PtinyHttpdDir=' form.
